methodology.title: Published cutoff history
methodology.description: Compare the entered priority date with the actual published Visa Bulletin cutoff and show past cutoff movement. The distance between dates is not a remaining wait time. No green-card approval dates or remaining wait times are predicted.
steps: Use chronological, sourced monthly Final Action Date or Dates for Filing cutoffs for the selected country and category.
For a dated cutoff, the entered priority date must be strictly earlier, not equal. Preserve Current (C) and Unavailable (U) as distinct published states.
Show past monthly cutoff changes, retaining stalls and retrogression rather than converting historical movement into future eligibility or approval dates.
Measure historical net cutoff movement across complete six-month windows only. Exclude windows containing Current, Unavailable, missing dates or missing months.
Do not infer a queue position, inventory, spillover, future visa supply, remaining wait time or green-card approval date.
limitations: Future movement depends on visa demand, supply, policy and agency decisions and can differ completely from prior movement. Historical movement does not predict a remaining wait time or green-card approval date.
No USCIS inventory or I-140 queue is estimated. Approved petitions do not directly equal people or visa demand, and a filing cutoff hides applicants who cannot file.
This dataset does not independently verify USCIS's monthly choice of the filing chart. Check the official USCIS page before filing I-485.
Meeting a Final Action Date removes only the cutoff constraint. It does not establish approval, a reserved visa number, case readiness or a processing duration.
For consular processing, the filing cutoff concerns assembly and submission of documents following National Visa Center instructions.
methodology.familyCategories: Family-sponsored preference categories show sourced cutoff history only; no remaining wait times or green-card approval dates are predicted.

sourceAccess.bulletins: Twenty-five contiguous official DOS bulletins include both Final Action Dates and Dates for Filing for five employment and five family preference categories across five chargeability areas. Canonical source and actual retrieval URLs are retained.
sourceAccess.inventory: The current USCIS data index returned HTTP 403 during research. No current inventory was imported or inferred.
sourceAccess.automation: GitHub Actions checks weekly. Official DOS HTML is fetched from travel.state.gov or its openly published adoption.state.gov/adoptions.state.gov hosts. Canonical sources and actual retrieval URLs are retained. All tracked cells and contiguous history are validated; errors preserve the published data. A monthly successful-check record does not change the data verification date.
